data.name: Portugal

sources.label: Freedom House: country electoral and political indicators, 2026 edition

legitimacy.summary:
Our assessment: Portugal has broadly credible and competitive national electoral institutions. The latest country indicators support meaningful voter choice, sound electoral rules and an opposition able to contest governing power. This is not a guarantee that every contest is flawless, nor a judgement about the popularity of any party.

Evidence baseline: Freedom in the World 2026, covering conditions in 2025. Our review date is not the date of an observer verdict on a later ballot; subsequent contests may require a separate assessment.

data.coverageNote: Selected records only. Earlier elections and additional result detail are still being added.

data.notes: The Democratic Alliance was listed as PSD/CDS in most districts and PSD/CDS/PPM in the Azores. Its 91 seats and 2,008,437 votes are combined; coalition votes are not assigned to individual member parties. Vote shares are as published by parliament and may reflect its final certified figures.
data.title: Assembly of the Republic

sources.label: Assembly of the Republic: 2025 election results and official map

data.summary: All 230 seats are recorded. The Democratic Alliance won 91, Chega 60 and the Socialist Party 58.
data.voteBasis: National party-list vote shares; alliance votes and seats are combined across its two ballot labels. Vote counts shown where confirmed by Portugal's parliament; minor zero-seat lists are omitted.
